text: Photography captures light through a camera to produce an image on film or a digital sensor. Two primary elements drive this mechanism: the shutter and the aperture. The shutter functions as a gate within the body, regulating the volume of light that reaches the interior. The aperture operates similarly but is located inside the lens; it varies its size to modulate light intake. Adjusting both components allows an operator to manage exposure levels and generate varied photographic results. Increasing the aperture opening reduces depth of field, rendering the background indistinct while sharpening the main subject. Conversely, decreasing the aperture opening expands depth of field, ensuring that foreground and background elements remain sharp.
